subject: math
title: Add and Subtract Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Like Denominators, Mixed Numbers and Word Problems
standard_text: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b. Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole. Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way. Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions with like denominators: break apart fractions, add and subtract with models, mixed numbers with renaming, and word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Same denominator: add or subtract the numerators. The denominator stays the same.
key_sub: The denominator is the size of the pieces, and it does not change: 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8, not 5/16. With mixed numbers, rename 1 whole when you need more pieces: 3 1/4 = 2 5/4.
body_html:
Add and subtract the same size pieces

When fractions have the same denominator, the pieces are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators (how many pieces). Keep the denominator (the size of the pieces).

A fraction like 58 is 5 pieces of 18: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 18. You can break it apart in more than one way.

Example

58 + 78 = ?

Add the numerators: 5 + 7 = 12. Keep eighths: 128. That is more than 1, because 88 = 1. So 128 = 1 48.

Answer: 128 = 1 48

Example

710 − 310 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 7 − 3 = 4. The pieces are still tenths.

Answer: 410

Mixed numbers

Add or subtract the fractions, then the whole numbers.

ProblemFractionsWhole numbersAnswer
2 15 + 1 3515 + 35 = 452 + 1 = 33 45
2 58 + 1 7858 + 78 = 128 = 1 482 + 1 + 1 = 44 48
4 56 − 1 2656 − 26 = 364 − 1 = 33 36

If the first fraction is too small to subtract from, rename 1 whole as 44, 88 and so on.

Example

3 14 − 1 34 = ?

Rename: 3 14 = 2 54. Fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1.

Answer: 1 24

On this page, answers keep the same denominator as the problem. 24 is right, and so is 12.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
28 + 38 = 516 (adding the denominators)The pieces stay eighths: 58
58 + 78 = 128, and stopping thereWhen asked for a mixed number, take out the whole: 1 48
2 58 + 1 78 = 3 48Add the 1 whole from 128: 4 48
3 14 − 1 34 = 2 24 (taking 14 from 34 instead)Rename 1 whole: 2 54 − 1 34 = 1 24
5 − 2 38 = 3 38Rename 5 as 4 88: the answer is 2 58

faq.q: How do you add fractions with the same denominator?
faq.a: Add the numerators and keep the denominator. For example, 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8, because 2 eighths and 3 eighths make 5 eighths.

faq.q: Why don't you add the denominators?
faq.a: The denominator tells the size of the pieces, and the size does not change when you put pieces together. Eighths plus eighths are still eighths, so 2/8 + 3/8 is 5/8, not 5/16.

faq.q: How do you subtract mixed numbers when the first fraction is smaller?
faq.a: Rename 1 whole as a fraction first. For 3 1/4 − 1 3/4, write 3 1/4 as 2 5/4, then subtract: 5/4 − 3/4 = 2/4 and 2 − 1 = 1, so the answer is 1 2/4.

faq.q: Do 4th graders have to simplify fractions?
faq.a: No. The Grade 4 standard asks students to add and subtract fractions with like denominators, so 4/8 is a correct answer. Writing it as 1/2 is also correct but not required.

items.q: 3 14 − 1 34 = ?
items.e: 14 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 3 14 = 2 54. Subtract the fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 24.

items.q: 5 25 − 2 45 = ?
items.e: 25 is less than 45, so rename 1 whole as 55: 5 25 = 4 75. Subtract the fractions: 75 − 45 = 35. Subtract the whole numbers: 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 2 35.

items.q: 4 16 − 1 56 = ?
items.e: 16 is less than 56, so rename 1 whole as 66: 4 16 = 3 76. Subtract the fractions: 76 − 56 = 26. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 26.

items.q: 6 310 − 3 710 = ?
items.e: 310 is less than 710, so rename 1 whole as 1010: 6 310 = 5 1310. Subtract the fractions: 1310 − 710 = 610. Subtract the whole numbers: 5 − 3 = 2. The answer is 2 610.

items.q: 5 − 2 38 = ?
items.e: There is no fraction to take 38 from, so rename 1 whole: 5 = 4 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 38 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 2 58.

items.q: Ben hiked 2 34 miles in the morning and 1 24 miles in the afternoon. How many miles did he hike in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 34 + 24 = 54. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 54 is more than 1: 54 = 1 14. So 3 + 1 14 = 4 14 miles.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Jack ate 38 of the pizza, and his sister ate 28 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: First find how much was eaten: 38 + 28 = 58. The whole pizza is 88. Left: 88 − 58 = 38.

items.q: A recipe for granola bars uses 23 cup of oats and 23 cup of raisins. How many cups is that in all?
items.e: Same denominator, so add only the numerators: 2 + 2 = 4. Keep the denominator 3: 43. That is more than 1. Take out 33 = 1, so 43 = 1 13 cups.

items.q: Kai drank 78 of a bottle of water. Ava drank 48 of a bottle the same size. How much more of a bottle did Kai drink than Ava?
items.e: “How much more” means subtract: 78 − 48. Same denominator, so subtract only the numerators: 7 − 4 = 3. Keep the denominator 8: 38.

items.q: Nora had a ribbon that was 4 14 feet long. She cut off 1 34 feet to wrap a gift. How many feet of ribbon are left?
items.e: 14 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 4 14 = 3 54. Subtract the fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 24 feet.

items.q: It rained 1 310 inches on Monday and 910 inch on Tuesday. How many inches of rain fell on the two days in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 310 + 910 = 1210. The whole number is 1. 1210 is more than 1: 1210 = 1 210. So 1 + 1 210 = 2 210 inches.

items.q: Sam practiced the piano for 1 34 hours on Saturday and 34 hour on Sunday. How many hours did he spend in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 34 + 34 = 64. The whole number is 1. 64 is more than 1: 64 = 1 24. So 1 + 1 24 = 2 24 hours.

items.q: A board is 6 feet long. Owen cuts off a piece that is 2 34 feet long. How long is the part that is left?
items.e: There is no fraction to take 34 from, so rename 1 whole: 6 = 5 44. Subtract the fractions: 44 − 34 = 14. Subtract the whole numbers: 5 − 2 = 3. The answer is 3 14 feet.

items.q: Mia ran 3 34 miles. Lily ran 2 14 miles. How much farther did Mia run than Lily?
items.e: “How much farther” means subtract. Subtract the fractions: 34 − 14 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 2 = 1. The answer is 1 24 miles.

items.q: Emma needs 2 13 cups of milk to make pancakes. She has 1 23 cups. How much more milk does she need?
items.e: Subtract what she has from what she needs. 13 is less than 23, so rename 1 whole as 33: 2 13 = 1 43. Subtract the fractions: 43 − 23 = 23. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 23 cup.

items.q: Omar hiked 1 410 miles in the morning and 2 510 miles in the afternoon. How many miles did he hike in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 410 + 510 = 910. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. Put them together: 3 910 miles.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Eli ate 26 of the pizza, and his sister ate 36 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: First find how much was eaten: 26 + 36 = 56. The whole pizza is 66. Left: 66 − 56 = 16.

items.q: A recipe for muffins uses 1 14 cups of flour and 34 cup of milk. How many cups is that in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 14 + 34 = 44. The whole number is 1. 44 = 1, so 1 + 1 = 2 cups.

items.q: Sofia and Grace are painting a fence. Sofia painted 912 of the fence, and Grace painted 512 of it. How much more of the fence did Sofia paint than Grace?
items.e: “How much more” means subtract: 912 − 512. Same denominator, so subtract only the numerators: 9 − 5 = 4. Keep the denominator 12: 412.

items.q: Maya had a ribbon that was 3 58 feet long. She cut off 1 28 feet to wrap a gift. How many feet of ribbon are left?
items.e: Subtract the fractions: 58 − 28 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 38 feet.

items.q: It rained 2 610 inches on Friday and 1 810 inches on Saturday. How many inches of rain fell on the two days in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 610 + 810 = 1410. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 1410 is more than 1: 1410 = 1 410. So 3 + 1 410 = 4 410 inches.

items.q: Zoe read for 1 23 hours on Saturday and 23 hour on Sunday. How many hours did she spend in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 23 + 23 = 43. The whole number is 1. 43 is more than 1: 43 = 1 13. So 1 + 1 13 = 2 13 hours.

items.q: A rope is 5 yards long. Noah cuts off a piece that is 1 58 yards long. How long is the part that is left?
items.e: There is no fraction to take 58 from, so rename 1 whole: 5 = 4 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 58 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 4 − 1 = 3. The answer is 3 38 yards.

items.q: Luis biked 4 210 miles. Ruby biked 1 610 miles. How much farther did Luis bike than Ruby?
items.e: “How much farther” means subtract. 210 is less than 610, so rename 1 whole as 1010: 4 210 = 3 1210. Subtract the fractions: 1210 − 610 = 610. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 610 miles.

items.q: Leo needs 3 14 cups of flour to make bread. He has 1 34 cups. How much more flour does he need?
items.e: Subtract what he has from what he needs. 14 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 3 14 = 2 54. Subtract the fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 24 cups.
